title: What one number stands for six years of enrolment?
description: A school's enrolment in six years in a row is shown as six bars. The board adds the enrolments in steps, divides by six, and checks the answer by multiplying it back.
teaching_notes: One idea: with large numbers, add in steps and write each running total, then share the total over the number of years. Watch for students who divide by the largest year or lose a thousand while adding.

video_script.why: The child has shared small totals equally and now does the same with the large numbers of a school's enrolment.
video_script.substitution: The total enrolment shared equally over six years gives the mean enrolment for one year.
video_script.anchor: Six bars for a school's enrolment in six years in a row: 1555, 1670, 1750, 2013, 2040 and 2126
video_script.payoff_line: The mean enrolment is one thousand eight hundred and fifty nine students a year

final_answer.spoken: one thousand eight hundred and fifty nine students per year

maths_rules: mean = total / number of years = 11154 / 6 = 1859 students
check: 1859 x 6 = 11154, the total; 1859 lies between 1555 and 2126
video_script.design: Six bars of different heights with their numbers. The board writes each running total, divides the last by six, and multiplies back.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a school building and six bars for six years, each bar labelled with its enrolment

marks.m1: the title card From your book appears
marks.m3: the six bars rise one after another, each with its enrolment
marks.m4: a question mark rises over the bars

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It gives the enrolment in a school during six years in a row.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The bars show the number of students in each year.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>What one number can stand for the enrolment of all six years?

beats.on_screen: the six bars stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child who is thinking

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the six bars slide into one tall stack, which is then cut into six equal parts

marks.g1: the six bars slide into one tall stack
marks.g2: the stack is cut into six equal parts

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>The mean shares the total equally over the six years.

marks.given: the six enrolments are written in a row
marks.g2: the third and fourth enrolments are underlined
marks.g3: the last two enrolments are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the enrolment in six years in a row was as follows.
One thousand five hundred and fifty five, and one thousand six hundred and seventy.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Then one thousand seven hundred and fifty, and two thousand and thirteen.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>Last, two thousand and forty, and two thousand one hundred and twenty six.

beats.on_screen: To find: the mean enrolment in the school during this period

marks.find: the words mean enrolment are underlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the mean enrolment in the school during this period.

marks.s1: the first two enrolments are added to 3225
marks.s2: the third and fourth enrolments are added, giving 4975 and 6988
marks.s3: the fifth and sixth enrolments are added, giving 9028 and 11154

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, add the enrolments in steps, and write each running total.
The first two years make three thousand two hundred and twenty five.
<bookmark mark='s2'/>Adding the third year makes four thousand nine hundred and seventy five.
The fourth year makes six thousand nine hundred and eighty eight.
<bookmark mark='s3'/>The fifth year makes nine thousand and twenty eight.
The sixth year makes eleven thousand one hundred and fifty four.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, mean = total ÷ number of years: 11154 ÷ 6 = 1859

marks.d1: the rule mean = total ÷ number of years is written

narration: <bookmark mark='d1'/>Step two, divide the total by the number of years, which is six.
<bookmark mark='d2'/>Eleven thousand one hundred and fifty four divided by six gives one thousand eight hundred and fifty nine.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, check: 1859 × 6 = 11154, the same as the total; 1859 lies between 1555 and 2126

marks.c1: the mean is repeated across the 6 years
marks.c2: the product 11154 is matched with the total

narration: <bookmark mark='c1'/>Step three, check by putting the answer back.
<bookmark mark='c2'/>One thousand eight hundred and fifty nine multiplied by six gives the total again.
The mean also lies between the smallest and the largest enrolment.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The mean enrolment is one thousand eight hundred and fifty nine students a year.
